question.text: In chromite ore, the oxidation number of iron and chromium are respectively.

solution.text: Actual composition of chromite ore<math><mo>(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">F</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">r</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub><mo>)</mo></math> is FeO.<math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">r</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></math>. In FeO, the oxidation state of Fe is +2 while in <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">r</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></math>, the oxidation state of Cr is +3.
